subject: cd
question: Why is LR parsing good and attractive? Also explain its demerits.
title: Powerful But Heavy
hook: What if a parser never had to guess and go back?
answer: Merit: handles virtually all programming-language constructs for which a context-free grammar can be written.
Merit: the most general non-backtracking shift-reduce method, yet as efficient as the others.
Merit: LR grammars are a proper superset of LL (predictive) grammars, so LR is more powerful.
Merit: detects a syntax error as early as possible in a left-to-right scan.

Demerits: too much work to build the tables by hand (needs a parser generator such as YACC); canonical LR(1) tables are very large; ambiguous grammars cause shift/reduce or reduce/reduce conflicts and must be rewritten.
